issue.title: JSDoc chokes on @param {String} headers['X-My-Header']

repository.name: jsdoc
repository.description: An API documentation generator for JavaScript.

issue.body:
Hi, I have a bit of a conundrum: I have a method that accepts an options object. A couple of the options are headers which use dashes instead of camel case. I'd like to run both JSDoc and eslint on my code, but I can't seem to find a way to document the options that makes both happy.

This works for JSDoc, but confuses eslint's [valid-jsdoc](http://eslint.org/docs/rules/valid-jsdoc) rule, causing my tests to fail:

``` js
/**
 * Example
 *
 * @param {Object} options
 * @param {String} [options.X-My-Header] custom header
 * @returns {*}
 */
function example(options) {
  // ...
}
```

The error from eslint is 

>   26:1  warning  Missing JSDoc parameter type for 'String'  valid-jsdoc

Meanwhile, this passes eslint, but then causes JSDoc to explode

``` js
/**
 * Example
 *
 * @param {Object} options
 * @param {String} [options['X-My-Header']] custom header
 * @returns {*}
 */
function example(options) {
  // ...
}
```

The error is

```
            paramRegExp = new RegExp('^(?:' + parentParam.name + '(?:\\[\\])*)\\.(.+)$');
                          ^

SyntaxError: Invalid regular expression: /^(?:options['X-My-Header'](?:\[\])*)\.(.+)$/: Range out of order in character class
    at new RegExp (native)
    at eval (eval at <anonymous> (/Users/nfriedly/watson-speech/node_modules/jsdoc/node_modules/underscore/underscore.js:1454:20), <anonymous>:19:27)
    at Array.forEach (native)
    at eval (eval at <anonymous> (/Users/nfriedly/watson-speech/node_modules/jsdoc/node_modules/underscore/underscore.js:1454:20), <anonymous>:11:12)
    at template (/Users/nfriedly/watson-speech/node_modules/jsdoc/node_modules/underscore/underscore.js:1461:21)
    at exports.Template.partial (/Users/nfriedly/watson-speech/node_modules/jsdoc/lib/jsdoc/template.js:60:29)
    at eval (eval at <anonymous> (/Users/nfriedly/watson-speech/node_modules/jsdoc/node_modules/underscore/underscore.js:1454:20), <anonymous>:56:14)
    at template (/Users/nfriedly/watson-speech/node_modules/jsdoc/node_modules/underscore/underscore.js:1461:21)
    at exports.Template.partial (/Users/nfriedly/watson-speech/node_modules/jsdoc/lib/jsdoc/template.js:60:29)
    at eval (eval at <anonymous> (/Users/nfriedly/watson-speech/node_modules/jsdoc/node_modules/underscore/underscore.js:1454:20), <anonymous>:207:14)
    at Array.forEach (native)
    at eval (eval at <anonymous> (/Users/nfriedly/watson-speech/node_modules/jsdoc/node_modules/underscore/underscore.js:1454:20), <anonymous>:205:10)
    at Array.forEach (native)
    at eval (eval at <anonymous> (/Users/nfriedly/watson-speech/node_modules/jsdoc/node_modules/underscore/underscore.js:1454:20), <anonymous>:10:10)
    at template (/Users/nfriedly/watson-speech/node_modules/jsdoc/node_modules/underscore/underscore.js:1461:21)
    at exports.Template.partial (/Users/nfriedly/watson-speech/node_modules/jsdoc/lib/jsdoc/template.js:60:29)
```

Arguably this is really an eslint issue, and I filled https://github.com/eslint/eslint/issues/5612 to resolve that, but I still figured you guys might want to know about it too. 

I think something simple like escaping `[` and `]` before creating the regex might be good enough, to keep JSDoc from exploding.

body: ESLint uses Doctrine as a parser for jsdoc, so I think you might've filed an issue in the wrong repository (jsdoc). I think the rule is complaining because you are trying to describe properties of an object, where your function accepts only one object. I'm actually not sure how this is supposed to work. @gyandeeps any ideas about the right way to do jsdoc comments for object properties of an argument?
I think he needs to define `options` using `@type` first and then simply say `{OptionsObject} [options]`.

OK, to give some expanded context, here's what the full JSDoc for that method looks like:

``` js
/**
 * Synthesize and play the supplied text over the computers speakers.
 *
 * Creates and returns a HTML5 `<audio>` element
 *
 * @param {Object} options
 * @param {String} options.token auth token
 * @param {String} options.text text to speak
 * @param {String} [options.voice=en-US_MichaelVoice] what voice to use - call getVoices() for a complete list.
 * @param {Number} [options.X-WDC-PL-OPT-OUT=0] set to 1 to opt-out of allowing Watson to use this request to improve it's services
 * @param {Boolean} [options.autoPlay=true] automatically play the audio
 * @returns {Audio}
 * @see module:watson-speech/text-to-speech/get-voices
 */
```

And JSDoc produces a table from that with each property listed: http://watson-developer-cloud.github.io/speech-javascript-sdk/master/module-watson-speech_text-to-speech_synthesize.html

The whole codebase uses this pattern, and except for hyphenated object keys, everything works swimmingly. But for hyphenated keys, JSDoc and ESLint/Doctrine seem to differ in what they'll accept. 

I'll try it with a `@type` and let you know if that works any better, but it probably won't be until Monday. 

I'll also take a look at Doctrine and probably file a bug there.

@nfriedly - thanks for sharing the larger snippet. Now I can definitely see this is an issue. This is most probably due to https://github.com/eslint/doctrine/issues/116

I'll keep this ticket here in ESLint open to track progress.

Opened a [PR to doctrine](https://github.com/eslint/espree/pull/265) to attempt to fix this. I've already tested that branch of doctrine with ESLint locally and can open a PR with tests covering this and bumping the doctrine version if that gets merged.
Changes merged to doctrine. Will finalize this PR when the next doctrine version is released.

issue.title: Fix: Update doctrine to allow hyphens in JSDoc names (fixes #5612)
